name: EEGManyLabs: Repication of Vogel & Machizawa (2004)
readme:
# EEGManyLabs - Replication Raw Dataset - Vogel & Machizawa (2004) # Raw Data This repository contains raw EEG data from the EEGManyLabs replication of the study: Vogel, E. K., & Machizawa, M. G. (2004) Neural activity predicts individual differences in visual working memory capacity. Nature, 428, 748–751. https://doi.org/10.1038/nature02447 BE AWARE - EEG data from multiple different sites. Recordings have different sampling rates, channel layouts, recording references, and have not been rereferenced. # Project description EEGManyLabs is a large scale, multi site replication project investigating influential EEG findings across laboratories. This dataset belongs to the replication of the Vogel and Machizawa (2004) visual working memory experiment, which introduced the Contralateral Delay Activity (CDA) as a neural marker of visual working memory capacity. The present repository contains raw EEG recordings organized according to the Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) standard. # Data format (BIDS) The dataset follows the BIDS specification for EEG data. A typical structure is: ``` sub-VogeXXXX/ eeg/ sub-Voge0001_coordsystem.json sub-Voge0001_electrodes.tsv sub-Voge0001_task-CDA_channels.tsv sub-Voge0001_task-CDA_eeg.eeg sub-Voge0001_task-CDA_eeg.vhdr sub-Voge0001_task-CDA_eeg.vmrk sub-Voge0001_task-CDA_events.tsv sub-Voge0001_task-CDA_eeg.json sub-Voge0001_task-Eye_channels.tsv sub-Voge0001_task-Eye_eeg.eeg sub-Voge0001_task-Eye_eeg.vhdr sub-Voge0001_task-Eye_eeg.vmrk sub-Voge0001_task-Eye_events.tsv sub-Voge0001_task-Eye_eeg.json ``` Files labeled `task-CDA` contain EEG data recorded during the visual working memory change detection task used in the replication of Vogel and Machizawa (2004). Files labeled `task-Eye` contain EEG recorded during a dedicated eye movement calibration procedure. These recordings are not used for CDA estimation but are included to support reliable detection of eye movements and control for ocular artifacts in the main task. The dataset is provided in the original acquisition format. The data are not filtered and not rereferenced. Sampling rates differ across laboratories, and multiple EEG recording systems were used. At some laboratories (University of Munster, North Dakota State University, Ohio State University, and the University of Zurich (Prof. Nicolas Langer)), eye tracker recordings were acquired and synchronized with the EEG. # Data download ```gin get EEGManyLabs/EEGManyLabs_Replication_VogelMachizawa2004_Raw```
```cd EEGManyLabs_Replication_VogelMachizawa2004_Raw```
Download selected files, e.g.
```gin get-content dataBIDS```
```gin get-content dataBIDS/participants.json```
```gin get-content dataBIDS/sub-Voge0001```
# Related publication Please cite the EEGManyLabs replication when using this dataset: Strzelczyk, D., Clayson, P. E., Sigurdardottir, H. M., et al. (2023). Contralateral delay activity as a marker of visual working memory capacity: A multi site registered replication. PsyArXiv. https://doi.org/10.31234/osf.io/shdea Strzelczyk, D., Clayson, P. E., Sigurdardottir, H. M., et al. (2026). Contralateral delay activity as a marker of visual working memory capacity: A multi site registered replication. Cortex. Additionally, cite the original study: Vogel, E. K., & Machizawa, M. G. (2004). Neural activity predicts individual differences in visual working memory capacity. Nature, 428, 748–751. https://doi.org/10.1038/nature02447 # Acknowledgements This dataset is part of the international EEGManyLabs collaboration involving multiple laboratories contributing data, analysis, and infrastructure to improve reproducibility in cognitive neuroscience. # Contact For questions regarding the dataset or BIDS structure, please contact: Dawid Strzelczyk
